statement: The supplied sources do not contain a derivation of the Laplace transform of a derivative. As stated and applied in the context of the capacitor constitutive differential equation i = C dv/dt, the Laplace transform of the derivative dv/dt is given by the relation \mathcal{L}\{dv/dt\} = s V(s) - V_0, where V(s) = \mathcal{L}\{v(t)\} and V_0 = v(0).

symbols.meaning: complex frequency variable of the Laplace transform
voltage across the capacitor terminals as a function of time
rate of change of electrical potential with respect to time
Laplace transform of voltage v(t), denoted \mathcal{L}\{v(t)\}
initial value of voltage at time t = 0, equal to v(0)
electric current through the capacitor as a function of time
Laplace transform of electric current i(t), denoted \mathcal{L}\{i(t)\}

properties.property: Converts the capacitor differential equation i = C dv/dt into the algebraic relation I(s) = C(s V(s) - V_0)
properties.why: direct substitution of the Laplace transform of the first derivative \mathcal{L}\{dv/dt\} = s V(s) - V_0 into the constitutive differential equation

properties.property: Allows solving for the transformed potential as V(s) = I(s)/(s C) + V_0/s
properties.why: algebraic rearrangement of the transformed equation I(s) = C(s V(s) - V_0)

properties.property: Yields the complex impedance of a capacitor Z(s) = 1/(s C)
properties.why: evaluating the ratio V(s)/I(s) under zero initial condition V_0 = 0

assumptions.assumption: The initial value V_0 = v(0) is well-defined and finite at t = 0.
assumptions.breaks_when: The function v(t) exhibits an undefined value, singularity, or impulse at the origin.

assumptions.assumption: The voltage function v(t) is differentiable on [0, \infty).
assumptions.breaks_when: The function v(t) is non-differentiable or has jump discontinuities.

assumptions.assumption: The Laplace transforms V(s) = \mathcal{L}\{v(t)\} and \mathcal{L}\{dv/dt\} converge in a common region of the complex s-plane.
assumptions.breaks_when: The function v(t) or its derivative grows faster than exponential order as t \to \infty.

failure_modes.mode: Omission of the initial condition term V_0
failure_modes.signature: I(s) is equated to s C V(s), failing to account for stored charge/energy at t = 0.
failure_modes.cause: Incorrectly assuming initial state is zero (V_0 = 0) in non-quiescent systems.

failure_modes.signature: Inconsistency between the time-domain derivative and transform-domain solution due to boundary ambiguity.
failure_modes.cause: Failure to distinguish between v(0^-) and v(0^+) when switching events or delta distributions occur at the origin.

canon_notes: canon expects a derivation but no source performs one, so laplace_transform_of_derivative is recorded as a definition
